## PARLIAMENT QUESTION: CANCER TREATMENT CENTRES/ HOSPITALS UNDER TATA MEMORIAL CENTRE AND DAE

### 

Posted On: 11 MAR 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi

Tata Memorial Centre under the Administrative control of DAE expanded in seven states by establishing 11 Hospital / Institutions to provide the comprehensive cancer care at Mumbai, Kharghar-New Mumbai, Punjab, Varanasi, Vizag, Muzaffarupur and Guwahati. TMC created the facility at Khopoli by tapping Indian system of medicine for drug discovery and for cheaper and less side effective drugs. Promotion of Indian and Traditional knowledge of Medicine. Cultivation and Conservation of Medicinal plants unique to India and a 200-bed state-of-the-art cancer hospital and research centre is being established at the NISER Campus, Jatni (Khurda district), Odisha.

Sr. No.  | Name of the Hospital  | City, State  | Date of commissioning  | Beds
1  | Tata Memorial Hospital  | Mumbai, Maharashtra  | 1941  | 650
12  | Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital  | Bhubaneswar, Odisha  | Expected 07/05/2026  | 200

 

The hospitals already established by Tata Memorial Centre are proof-of-concept that such a network can be created and can serve as models for developing more hubs and spokes by the State governments. Tata Memorial Centre is currently in the phase of consolidating its network, especially the non-Mumbai units, to achieve the high level of excellence that TMC Mumbai is renowned for. This consolidation comprises painstaking creation and assimilation of expert human resources in the new units of TMC, creating healthcare delivery pathways that have been honed in Mumbai TMC over decades of its existence, establishing the information technology (IT) backbone on which all TMC units run, creating an enabling ecosystem (example residential accommodation for staff, trainees and patients), and, maintaining and enhancing the infrastructure required to deliver high-quality cancer care.

Initiatives such as TMC’s National Cancer Grid could be a vehicle for technical input, such as resource-stratified guidelines, pathology reporting standards, virtual tumor boards, traveling school of pathology and nursing, etc, for progressive development of hubs and spokes. Tata Memorial Centre could also take the lead in creating an oncology-focused electronic medical record platform for widespread adoption by cancer institutions in India. This will be a significant step in enabling not only seamless data collection but also uniform standards of care throughout the country. Further, as part of the National Cancer Grid we have 380 cancer centres, research organizations and patient groups. However, the NCG does not have a hub and spoke model. The coordinating centre which is in Tata Memorial Hospital runs various activities across the member centres to strengthen cancer care in the country through quality improvement, standardization, manpower training and research.

Today is a special day for all of us at Small Animal Hospital, Mumbai (SAHM), as we take another significant step towards fulfilling the vision of our Chairman Emeritus, the Late Mr Ratan N Tata, of becoming a true tertiary care hospital for small animals in Mumbai. As part of our efforts to take this vision forward, we have entered into agreements with leading specialists in the fields of ophthalmology and oncology to establish and operate full-fledged departments at SAHM. From 28 September 2026, The Eye Vet will operate a full veterinary ophthalmology department and The Cancer Vet, a full oncology department alongside it, at Small Animal Hospital, Mumbai. Both departments will provide the complete range of specialised services, including surgeries and chemotherapy, on-site at SAHM, under the overall oversight of SAHM. This will significantly enhance the spectrum of clinical activities that SAHM can offer in these specialties.

To enhance the facilities for tertiary care of cancer, the Central Government is implementing Strengthening of Tertiary Care for Cancer Scheme, under which setting up of 19 State Cancer Institutes (SCIs) and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres (TCCCs) have been approved.

Chennai: Iswarya Hospital inaugurated the Iswarya Cancer Centre at its OMR Taramani campus on Sunday. "One of the biggest challenges we face is late diagnosis, which significantly reduces survival outcomes. Raipur, August 16: Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai on Sunday inaugurated the CARE Cancer Institute at Ramkrishna CARE Hospitals, Raipur, expanding access to advanced and comprehensive cancer treatment in the state.

The new institute has been developed as an integrated cancer-care centre offering services ranging from diagnosis and treatment planning to surgery, medical oncology, radiation therapy, bone marrow transplantation, nuclear medicine, supportive care and palliative care.

The launch assumes significance amid a growing cancer burden in Chhattisgarh. According to estimates cited by the hospital, the state recorded around 31,553 cancer cases in 2025, compared with 30,763 cases in 2024 — equivalent to nearly 100 new cases a day.
